name: Nahbi
overview: Nahbi was a male member of the tribe of Naphtali, known primarily for being one of the twelve spies sent by Moses to explore the land of Canaan. His role as a spy is noted in Numbers 13:14, emphasizing his participation in this significant event in Israel's history. The Scriptures identify him specifically as a representative of the tribe of Naphtali.
namesAndTitles: The name Nahbi, as recorded in Numbers 13:14, may mean 'hidden' or 'timid,' though this is presented as a possible interpretation rather than a definitive meaning. No additional titles or names are associated with him in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Nahbi is identified as the son of Vophsi, according to Numbers 13:14. Beyond this paternal relationship, Scripture does not provide further details about his family or other relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Nahbi's significance lies in his role as one of the twelve spies chosen to scout the Promised Land, representing the tribe of Naphtali. This mission was crucial in the unfolding narrative of Israel's journey and God's promise to bring His people into the land. His inclusion among the spies highlights his trusted position within his tribe and Israel as a whole.
